clue.text: One can barely finish one's stage act

definitions.text: One can barely finish one's stage act

parts.words: One can barely finish one's stage act
parts.note: a performer whose act ends with them almost naked; 'barely' is the pun

explanation.surface: A nervous performer can hardly get through their turn on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' reads as 'hardly', but the performer really does finish bare, wearing next to nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This performer sheds clothing throughout the show, ending it almost nude.

clue.text: Christmas Eve was such a quiet night

definitions.text: Christmas Eve was such a quiet night

parts.words: Christmas Eve was such a quiet night
parts.note: a famous carol title calls the night of Christ's birth hushed and without noise

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a peaceful Christmas Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to the carol 'Silent Night', about the night of Christ's birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiet, noiseless night is a hushed one, as the well-known carol title puts it.

clue.text: Any number in America are favouring gender equality

indicators.note: one piece sits within another, here the number letter goes inside the country's initials

parts.note: US is short for United States, America
N is the algebraic symbol for an unspecified number
to be is to exist, so 'are' means exist

explanation.surface: A claim that most people in the US support equality of the sexes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who treats men and women alike is not sexist, the opposite of discriminating by sex.

clue.text: Inferior, so joint bottom?

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning joint or shared, as in co-owner
arse is British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A rude query whether a shared backside is second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: ARSE is British slang for the bottom; a crude word fits a crude answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse goods are rough and of low quality, so second-rate.

clue.text: Offer more: you'll get a lot from it

definitions.meaning: to bid higher than a rival

definitions.text: you'll get a lot from it
definitions.meaning: at auction, beating the other bids wins you the lot being sold

explanation.surface: Advice that giving extra brings plenty back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' sounds like 'plenty', but it is an auction lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating a rival's bid means offering a higher price, which wins the auction item.

clue.text: Love to gather together by word of mouth

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
to rally is to come together for a common cause

explanation.surface: Affection brings people together, spread by talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done orally is spoken rather than written, passed on in speech.

clue.text: Having expectations of a new horse?

definitions.text: Having expectations of a new horse?

parts.words: Having expectations of a new horse?
parts.note: 'expecting' means pregnant, and a mare carrying a young horse is described this way

explanation.surface: Someone hopes great things from a horse just bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having expectations' is pregnancy, as in 'expecting'; the new horse is unborn.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant mare carries a young horse, a description used for breeding stock.

clue.text: Sixteen kings and finally one woman

parts.note: Louis XVI was the sixteenth French king of that name, so sixteen kings all bore it

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word one

explanation.surface: A list of sixteen monarchs ends with a single woman.
explanation.walkthrough: France had more than sixteen kings named Louis; 'Sixteen' points to the famous Louis XVI.
explanation.definitionFit: Louise is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Left organised chain gang

definitions.meaning: the left of British politics is represented chiefly by the ...
a chain gang is a group put to labour, organised like a political party

explanation.surface: A prison work crew has been set up and gone away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Labour Party is the main British party of the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The main left-wing British party; also, punningly, a group set to hard work.

clue.text: 'Farewell', clutching one's overnight bag

indicators.note: clutching means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: vale is Latin for goodbye
one's means one is, I plus IS

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye while holding their travel bag.
explanation.walkthrough: VALE is Latin for 'farewell', used in English for a formal goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small travelling case, suited to a night away.

clue.text: Cohort that gets on together

definitions.meaning: a cohort is a group of people of similar age, as in a study
'gets on' means grows older, so this group ages together

explanation.surface: A group of people who are friendly with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets on' reads as 'is friendly', but it means grows old.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of people born around the same time forms a single band of years.

clue.text: Knocking back lager is a slight mistake

indicators.note: knocking back sounds like drinking, but it means the word for lager is read backwards

parts.note: Pils is a pale lager, short for Pilsner

explanation.surface: Downing beer counts as only a small error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' looks like drinking the lager; it reverses PILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small error, like a slip of the tongue.

clue.text: Grabbed something simple and sat back

parts.note: took means grabbed or seized
it can stand for an unnamed thing
easy means simple, not difficult

explanation.surface: Someone seized an easy option and relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax and avoid effort is to rest, lean back and do little.

clue.text: When travelling, spot erratic old creature

indicators.note: travelling means moving about, so the letters of the two words move into a new order

explanation.surface: On a journey you notice something wandering about.
explanation.definitionFit: This three-horned dinosaur lived millions of years ago, an ancient animal.

clue.text: Unambiguous measure of volume curate's drunk

parts.note: cl is the abbreviation for centilitre

indicators.note: a drunk person is in disorder, so the letters of curate are mixed up

parts.note: curate's is curate is; the word curate supplies the fodder

explanation.surface: The curate has clearly had a measured quantity of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in "curate's" is 'is', a link; the surface makes the curate the drinker, but he only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clear-cut is plain and definite, leaving no doubt.

clue.text: Stop trying to stuff suitcase?

definitions.meaning: literally, to pack things into a case

explanation.surface: Give up trying to cram the luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack it in is British slang for quitting; literally it means filling a case.

clue.text: Villains have run over visitor, severing foot

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the foot of a down entry is its end, so the final letter is cut away

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: Criminals drove over a guest and cut off his foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'severing foot' cuts the last letter, T, from GUEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogues are dishonest scoundrels, wrongdoers.

clue.text: No 1 saver

parts.note: in football the keeper traditionally wears the number 1 shirt and saves shots

explanation.walkthrough: 'saver' suggests money; the saves are of shots, and the No 1 is the shirt number.
explanation.definitionFit: The football keeper wears the number one shirt and stops shots on target.

clue.text: Rely on nerve, where there are many dead men

definitions.text: where there are many dead men

indicators.note: on means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage
to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: Depend on courage at a place with many corpses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dead men' is slang for empty bottles; the definition names a recycling bin for glass, common at British supermarkets.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty bottles, jokingly called dead men, pile up in this recycling container.

clue.text: Additionally, where one may apply a shoehorn

definitions.meaning: ... is an idiom meaning as well

definitions.text: where one may apply a shoehorn
definitions.meaning: a shoehorn helps the foot into footwear, literally to the boot

explanation.surface: Someone also uses a shoehorn somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means besides or as well; literally, a shoehorn is used at footwear.

clue.text: Young pet: one's anxious to have many

definitions.meaning: to have ... is a British idiom for being very worried

explanation.surface: A worried owner wants lots of baby animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having kittens' is British slang for being very nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby cat is a common household animal; and anxious people are said to have these.

clue.text: Store where hens sleep

definitions.meaning: the ... is a British chain of cooperative shops
a cage or pen for poultry

explanation.surface: A storehouse where chickens roost.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British cooperative supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooperative shop; also a pen for keeping poultry overnight.

clue.text: In pain after bathing?

parts.note: bathing suggests water, but sunbathing leaves skin sore and red

explanation.surface: Someone hurts after a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bathing' suggests water, but the bath is in sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Too long in sunshine leaves skin red and sore, the result of sunbathing carelessly.

clue.text: Last to shoot weapon: it's not important

indicators.note: last to asks for the closing letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a rifle is a gun

explanation.surface: The final person to fire a gun says it doesn't matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a thing of little value or significance, a mere nothing.

clue.text: Appear to embarrass

definitions.meaning: to show someone up is to make them look foolish

explanation.surface: Turning up just to humiliate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to arrive and to humiliate someone in public.

clue.text: Carefully determine what's cooked in feed

indicators.note: cooked means altered or falsified, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Working out exactly what has been prepared in animal food.
explanation.definitionFit: To define something is to fix its meaning or limits precisely.
